title: Chavivi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: This is what Rav called his uncle Rabbi Chiyya, as explained in his entry. Hyman connects it with the language of Targum Onkelos, which renders דוד אהרן (Aaron’s uncle) as אחבוהי דאהרן; in short, chaviv.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Metsudah 2009 digital Onkelos on Leviticus 10:4 has אח אבוהי דאהרן, “Aaron’s father’s brother.” Hyman supplies the compressed אחבוהי דאהרן and derives chaviv from it. The lexical comparison supports the uncle sense, without proving Hyman’s proposed shortening as a historical derivation.

The actual Onkelos Leviticus 10:4 wording אח אבוהי דאהרן supplies the uncle comparison. Hyman’s compressed form and proposed derivation are preserved as his explanation, without asserting a demonstrated historical shortening.
